question: A country's fiscal policy is aimed at reducing the budget deficit. What is the effect on government spending?
options: Government spending will decrease but at a slower rate
Government spending will increase
Government spending will remain unchanged
Government spending will decrease

question: A firm's demand curve shifts to the right due to a rise in consumer income. What will be the effect on the demand curve of a luxury good?
options: The demand curve will shift to the left initially but then to the right
The demand curve will remain unchanged
The demand curve will shift further to the right
The demand curve will shift to the left

question: A country's ______________ is the sum of its net imports and its capital outflow.
options: foreign exchange inflow
net foreign exchange expenditure
foreign exchange outflow
net foreign exchange earnings

question: A country's monetary policy is aimed at reducing inflation. What is the effect on the money supply?
options: The money supply will decrease
The money supply will increase
The money supply will decrease but at a slower rate
The money supply will remain unchanged

question: A firm operates in a perfectly competitive market. What is the effect on the firm's supply curve of a decline in input costs?
options: The supply curve will shift to the right
The supply curve will shift to the left
The supply curve will remain unchanged
The supply curve will shift to the left initially but then to the right

question: A firm is a price maker in a monopolistic market. What is the effect on the firm's revenue of a 10% increase in price?
options: Revenue will decrease
Revenue will increase by less than 10%
Revenue will increase
Revenue will remain unchanged

question: An oligopolistic firm will choose a price that is higher than the one that would maximize profit if there were no other firms in the market. What is the reason for this?
options: The firm needs to set a price that is sufficiently high to increase profit
The firm needs to set a price that is sufficiently low to increase demand
The firm needs to set a price that is sufficiently high to attract existing customers
The firm needs to set a price that is sufficiently high to deter potential new entrants
